record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study develops scaling relationships for safety-probe error, a different quantity from held-out language-model pretraining loss. It also compares probe-allocation decisions against forms from Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al., without testing their pretraining-loss claims.
record.gate_note: The measured outcome is safety-probe error (1 − AUROC), not language-model held-out cross-entropy. The paper cites prior pretraining scaling-law results and uses related functional forms as comparators for decisions about probing; those cited results are not extracted as rows. Its safety-probe results are recorded below as related findings with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study's outcome is safety-probe error (1 − AUROC) as a function of monitored-model size and probe-label count. This is not held-out pretraining loss, compute-optimal pretraining allocation, or downstream task performance of the language models themselves. The Kaplan and Hoffmann functional forms appear only as comparator rules for probe-allocation decisions (R16). The study borrows scaling-law methodology for a new quantity, probe readability, and does not test any claim version. The classification as uses_without_test/T4 is reasonable; one could argue it is closer to T6 (cites and borrows form only), but no version is tested either way.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that probe error follows a size power law and a label law across tasks, families and probe architectures, with only constants changing. They conclude these laws can predict larger-model probe error, guide the choice between more labels and a bigger model, and guide probe-architecture choice. They frame probe error as the counterpart of test loss, a new quantity rather than a test of pretraining laws.
record.recipe_differences: The original studies measure language-model held-out pretraining loss and parameter/token/compute trade-offs. This study measures AUROC-derived safety-probe error over monitored-model size and probe-label count, using linear and CC++ probes.
record.method_sensitivity: Fitted constants differ by model family and task; the label-law form differs by probe architecture. For the last-token probe, the fitted steepness is g = 0.61 on Qwen2.5 Truth, while CC++ is generally close to g = 1 but has larger departures on General harm and Prompt injection. The authors also report that estimates of the size-law slope settle as more sizes and a wider size span are included.

fits_no_version.finding: Safety-probe error falls as a power law in monitored-model size, with a label-count law converging to that floor. Constants vary by task, family and probe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Probe error (1 − AUROC) on safety tasks follows a size power law and a Hill-type label law across tested families, tasks and probe architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe-error laws fitted on smaller family members predict the next size: within 0.02 in 72% of cases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Probe-error scaling laws extrapolate one size up within a family.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe error decreases with post-training and with pretraining progress.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-training and further pretraining lower safety-probe error in OLMo-3 and Qwen2.5.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe-error law constants (α) are unstable on narrow size spans and settle once the span reaches about ten-fold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitted probe-error exponents depend on the span of model sizes in the fit.

record.problems: The evidence concerns safety-probe error, not the claim’s pretraining-loss measure. The main size-law evidence is limited by available released dense-family sizes; OLMo-3 has only two main-family sizes and Ministral-3 three. The authors note that deployments may involve post-trained models and that the allocation-cost analysis counts parameters × labels but not label prices or other deployment costs. Seed-based intervals are reported, but several extrapolation and auxiliary results give no uncertainty interval.
record.rows_left_out: The paper contains many additional probe-setting and supplementary comparisons, including per-layer and position choices, head-size comparisons, all individual extrapolation cells, and additional checkpoint/model results. These do not measure any claim version’s specified pretraining-loss or compute-optimal-allocation outcome; the rows retained cover the central probe-scaling findings and reported extensions relevant to the claim’s subject.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute is never measured.
No extrapolation of pretraining loss. Extrapolation concerns probe error only (R15).
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation for pretraining. R16 is probe-label allocation.
No language-model shape variation at fixed parameter count affecting pretraining loss. Appendix E.4 relates probe error to layers and width, not pretraining loss.
No other-modality or training-regime loss scaling.
Probe error is a readout of activations, not model downstream-task performance.
Fit-dependence is studied for probe-error laws (span, exponent of N, g), not for pretraining-loss laws.

record.verdict_notes: Hypothetical future-dated preprint. The original-source pretraining laws are cited only as motivation and as comparator forms. No row bears on any version, so no verdict labels are given. The record's handling is correct overall; the only change is flagging R16 as a method comparison.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures safety-probe error, not held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, training tokens or training compute.
It predicts safety-probe error for larger monitored models, not pretraining loss of larger language-model training runs.
It considers model size and probe-label count, not a fixed language-model training-compute budget and the optimal parameter/token allocation.
Probe architecture is compared, but the study does not test how language-model depth, width or other architecture choices affect pretraining loss at fixed parameter count.
The tasks are safety-probing tasks on language-model activations; the study does not test scaling of pretraining loss across modalities or training regimes.
Probe error is not downstream task performance of the language models, nor is it related to their pretraining loss.
The paper studies fit choices for safety-probe error laws, not setup- or fitting-dependence of the pretraining-loss laws or compute-optimal parameter/token split.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 family, CC++ probe on Truth
rows.operation_detail: Fit probe error against parameter count at 10⁶ training labels.
rows.measure: Probe error E = 1 − AUROC and power-law fit E(N) = A N^−α
rows.value: Error falls from 0.18 at 0.5B to 0.056 at 72B; fit A = 0.15, α = 0.22, R² = 0.94 on log E, and no model is more than 0.012 from the line.
rows.note: The result concerns probe error, not pretraining cross-entropy.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 family, CC++ probe on Truth
rows.operation_detail: Fit probe error as a joint function of monitored-model size and number of probe-training labels.
rows.measure: Probe error learning curve and fitted half-distance label count D0
rows.baseline: Chance error 0.5 and the size-law floor E(N)
rows.value: D0 falls from 8,200 labels at 0.5B to 240 at 72B; the fitted label law uses B = 3,400 and D0 = B/√N. The joint law has mean RMS deviation 0.030 over 70 measurements, versus 0.017 with a separate D0 for each model; worst deviation is 0.115.
rows.uncertainty: Slope of log D0 against log N is −0.51, standard error 0.15
rows.note: Labels here train probes, not language-model pretraining.
rows.check: Locator is fine. Note that D0 per model is a fitted quantity; the reported B = 3,400 is rounded from 3,427 in Table 22.

rows.subject: Qwen3.5 family, CC++ probe on Truth
rows.operation_detail: Fit the probe-error size law and evaluate the joint size/label law.
rows.measure: Probe error against parameters and labels
rows.value: Each doubling of model size multiplies probe error by 0.76. The joint law deviates from measurements by 0.015 on average and 0.045 at worst; B = 404.
rows.note: Family-level fit reported across its models.

rows.subject: Five model families, last-token probe on Truth
rows.size_stated: 20 dense base models across five families

rows.measure: Probe error against parameters and number of labels

rows.subject: Dense model families with at least four sizes, safety probes
rows.size_stated: Qwen2.5, Qwen3.5 and Gemma-4; predictions for next larger family member
rows.operation_detail: Fit probe scaling laws on the smallest models in a family and predict the next model’s probe error.
rows.measure: Absolute error between predicted and measured probe error
rows.baseline: Straight-line probe-error trend against log N: 54% within 0.02
rows.value: The scaling laws predict the next model’s probe error within 0.02 in 72% of cases and within 0.05 in 97%; on Qwen2.5, predictions within 0.02 rise from 7 of 12 at k = 3 to 10 of 12 at k = 6.
rows.note: Prediction concerns safety-probe error, not the pretraining loss of larger runs.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5, CC++ probe
rows.size_stated: 0.5B to 14B fitted; comparison includes larger-model options
rows.operation_detail: Compare rules for choosing more probe labels versus a larger monitored model at a target probe error.

conditions.value: 45 cases where one option is at least twofold cheaper

rows.measure: Share of decisions selecting the cheaper option
rows.baseline: Hoffmann additive form 38%; Kaplan joint form 44%
rows.value: The study’s probe-error laws choose the cheaper option in 73% of cases.
rows.note: The compared forms are used to choose probe configurations; this is not a test of compute-optimal language-model pretraining allocation.
rows.check: The Hoffmann additive and Kaplan joint forms are refitted to probe-error cells and used as comparators for probe-allocation choices. The 73% vs 38%/44% figures compare the study's own method with other rules, not a test of V3. The row should be marked as a method comparison, not a finding about compute-optimal pretraining allocation.

rows.subject: OLMo-3 7B and 32B base and post-trained checkpoints
rows.stage_stated: base, SFT, DPO and final post-trained checkpoints
rows.operation_detail: Compare last-token probe error across post-training stages.
rows.measure: Probe error
rows.value: Post-training lowers probe error at every label budget. At 10⁶ labels, 7B falls from 0.111 to 0.096 and 32B from 0.072 to 0.062. At 10³ labels, error falls from 0.21 to 0.14–0.16 at 7B and 0.15 to 0.10–0.11 at 32B.
rows.note: The paper states that the gain is already present after supervised fine-tuning.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 Instruct family, last-token probe on Truth
rows.operation_detail: Fit probe-error size and label laws to post-trained checkpoints.
rows.measure: Probe error against parameters and labels
rows.baseline: Base models at the same sizes and label budget
rows.value: At 10⁵ labels, Instruct probe error is 0.60 to 0.87 times the base-model error. The size-law exponent is α = 0.30 for Instruct versus 0.27 for base. The label-law fit has B = 16, g = 0.53, RMS miss 0.025, and explains 90% of variance across cells.
rows.note: These are probe-error scaling results on post-trained models.

rows.subject: OLMo-3 intermediate pretraining checkpoints, 7B and 32B
rows.stage_stated: intermediate pretraining checkpoints and released base models
rows.operation_detail: Measure probe error across training checkpoints.
rows.measure: Probe error over pretraining steps
rows.value: For 7B, error falls from 0.286 after 10,000 steps to 0.151 at the end of stage 1, 0.105 at the end of stage 2, and 0.111 in the released base model. For 32B, it falls from 0.177 after 15,000 steps to 0.103 at the end of stage 1 and 0.072 in the released base model.
rows.note: The outcome is probe error over the monitored model’s training checkpoints.
rows.check: Probe error falls over OLMo-3 pretraining checkpoints. This is probe readability versus training steps, not held-out pretraining loss, so it does not bear on V1 despite the pretraining-progress axis.

rows.subject: Nemotron-H and Qwen1.5 families, last-token probe on Truth
rows.operation_detail: Fit probe-error size laws in two additional dense model families.
rows.measure: Probe-error size-law exponent α
rows.baseline: Five main families, reported range α = 0.05 to 0.47
rows.value: Nemotron-H has α = 0.42 and Qwen1.5 has α = 0.33; Qwen1.5 probe error is 0.14 to 0.29 and lies above other families at similar sizes.
rows.note: The authors report both additional families as following the size-law form.
